rationale: The BOOK ENTRY defines 'life (the life)' as covenant existence — life lived walking in the Way according to God's law — and prints exactly four texts. Deuteronomy 30:19-20 explicitly frames life as the covenant choice ('choose life... love the LORD... obey his voice... cleave unto him: for he is thy life'). Leviticus 18:5 states the mechanism directly: keeping God's statutes is how a man 'shall live in them.' Matthew 7:14 makes conduct ('the narrow way') the thing that 'leadeth unto life,' which is precisely the entry's claim that the walking produces the existence. John 14:6 is the only ambiguous witness, and the chapter supplies a coherent derivation: 'the way' is defined at its first occurrence as covenant conduct (Gen 18:19), and 'the life' as the existence that conduct yields, with Christ as its embodiment. The strongest counter — 'the life' as eternal, divine zōē given through Christ, with the definite form as a christological title — carries John 14:6 comfortably, but it cannot unify the other three printed texts without bifurcating 'life' into separate senses (covenantal-Deuteronomic vs. Johannine), which is exactly the move the entry avoids. Notably, the common interpretation itself (Response A, alternative 5) recognizes the covenantal-choice reading grounded in Deut 30:15-20 and Lev 18:5 as a legitimate, common sense of the term; the entry simply makes that sense the definition and shows the Johannine title cohering with it. No supplied text is left unexplained by the entry's core; the counter's advantages lie in texts not printed with the entry (John 3:16, 17:3, 1 John 5:11-12). On the actual cited evidence, the book's identification explains more with fewer unsupported steps.
book_core_identification: 'The life' is covenant existence — the mode of existence that flows from and consists in walking in the Way (covenant conduct) according to God's law, embodied perfectly in Christ.
book_secondary_elaborations: The life is produced by walking 'in the Way' (conduct yields existence, per Matt 7:14 and Lev 18:5)
The standard of that walking is God's law (per Deut 30:19-20 and Lev 18:5)
chapter_only_objections: The claim that Hebrews 10:20 prosphatos means 'freshly slain' rests on etymology; in Koine usage the word had generalized to 'recent/new,' so 'every major translation flattens it' overstates the case.
The identification of the flaming sword of Genesis 3:24 as the word of God 'preserving' rather than barring the way runs against the immediate narrative context of exclusion from the garden.
The uniform-symbol axiom (a definition given once holds everywhere) is asserted rather than demonstrated for 'light,' 'tree,' 'lion,' and 'beast' as deployed in this chapter.
The chapter's reading of 'no man cometh unto the Father but by me' as 'the original covenant road now named' is a theological application beyond what the glossary entry asserts.
The chapter's equation 'the truth = the law' (Ps 119:142) and 'light = the law lived visibly' are separate symbol claims defended elsewhere, not assertions of this entry.

Pauline usage of Lev 18:5 (Rom 10:5; Gal 3:12) sets 'the righteousness of the law' in contrast to faith-righteousness; the chapter does not engage this counter-application, though the entry's definitional use of the verse is independent of it.
strongest_counter_interpretation: 'The life,' especially in the definite Johannine form, is eternal, divine life (zōē) — a qualitatively different existence given by God through Jesus Christ, consisting in saving relationship and union with God, beginning now and consummated in resurrection; 'the Life' functions as a christological title (John 14:6; 11:25; 1:4; 1 John 5:11-12), and this divine life is received as a gift of grace rather than constituted by law-observance.
counter_core_identification: 'The life' = eternal divine life sourced in and identical with Christ, granted to believers by faith as gift and union with God, not defined by Torah-conduct.
material_core_denial: The counter denies that 'the life' is constituted by covenant law-keeping: in mainstream teaching eternal life is a gracious gift received by faith, and defining it as 'the life lived walking according to God's law' is held to invert the relation between obedience and life (obedience as fruit of life, not its constitution).
counter_case: John 14:6 in Johannine context presents Christ as personally being the life, paralleling John 11:25 and 1:4, favoring a christological-title reading over a covenant-conduct abstraction.
Deut 30:20 says 'he [the LORD] is thy life' — the referent of life is God himself, relationally, not the practice of law-keeping as such.
Pauline usage (Rom 10:5; Gal 3:12) treats Lev 18:5 as the emblem of a law-life principle contrasted with faith, suggesting the NT does not straightforwardly define 'the life' by statute-keeping.
The broader canonical witness (John 3:16; 17:3; 1 John 5:11-12; Col 3:4) presents life as gift and relationship 'in the Son,' texts the covenant-conduct definition does not foreground.
book_explanatory_advantages: Unifies all four printed texts under a single definition: Deut 30:19-20, Lev 18:5, and Matt 7:14 all explicitly bind life to covenant obedience/conduct, and John 14:6 is read consistently with them rather than in isolation.

Explains the definite article and the sequence of John 14:6 ('the way... the life') via the derived Old Testament definition of 'the way' as covenant conduct (Gen 18:19), so that 'the life' is the existence that way produces — matching Matt 7:14's 'way which leadeth unto life' verbatim.
Explains Prov 3:18 and Prov 6:23 ('reproofs of instruction are the way of life') where law, way, and life are strung on one thread.
Accounts for the earliest name of the movement ('the Way,' Acts 24:14) as covenant conduct per the law and prophets.
Deut 30:20's 'he is thy life' is accommodated: cleaving to the LORD in covenant is the content of the existence, and the chapter affirms Christ as the embodiment of that life.
counter_explanatory_advantages: Better fits the wider Johannine corpus not printed with the entry (John 3:16; 5:24-26; 17:3; 1 John 5:11-12), where life is possessed 'in the Son' by belief.
Handles Pauline polemic against life-by-law (Rom 10:5; Gal 3:12) without tension.
Matches the dominant historic reading of 'the Life' as a christological title across traditions.
decisive_sources: Deuteronomy 30:19-20 — life explicitly identified with loving, obeying, and cleaving to the LORD under covenant
Leviticus 18:5 — keeping statutes is the stated condition of living 'in them'
Matthew 7:14 — the way (conduct) is what 'leadeth unto life,' directly encoding the entry's conduct-yields-existence claim
Chapter derivation of 'the way' from Genesis 18:19 and Acts 24:14, making John 14:6 cohere with the three Old Testament witnesses
unresolved_objections: The entry does not address how its definition relates to Pauline texts that cite Lev 18:5 contrastively (Rom 10:5; Gal 3:12); this does not defeat the definitional claim on the printed texts but remains an open theological tension.
Deut 30:20's 'he is thy life' locates life in the LORD personally; the entry's conduct-centered phrasing carries this only via the chapter's gloss that the covenant relationship is the existence.
The wider Johannine gift-of-life texts (John 3:16; 17:3) are not integrated in the printed entry, though they are outside its cited scope.
